operations.summary: Price a link in mobile money
operations.description:
What the payer will be charged, before any prompt is raised. Safe to call on every change of country or amount: **nothing is sent to anyone's phone.**

On a link with an amount baked in, send neither `amount` nor `fiatAmount` — the invoice is authoritative and both are ignored. On an OPEN link one of them is required: `fiatAmount` is the better choice, because the payer is then prompted for exactly the figure they typed rather than one derived by converting to crypto and back.

params.name: currency
params.description: The market to price in. Omit it and the country is inferred from `phone`. **NGN is not supported**: Nigeria settles by bank transfer and has no prompt to push.

params.name: phone
params.description: Used only to infer the market when `currency` is absent.

params.name: fiatAmount
params.description: Open links only: what the payer pays, in the market's currency.

params.name: amount
params.description: Open links only: a crypto target instead.

operations.summary: Raise the payment prompt
operations.description:
Sends a mobile-money prompt to the payer's phone. Returns as soon as it is out — `status` is `processing`, never `completed`. Poll the order; the payer may take a minute or never approve.

The crypto lands at the LINK's recipient address, which is why no address is accepted here.

Two abuse brakes sit in front of this, and neither touches the merchant's account: one counts abandoned prompts per phone number, the other counts them per link across distinct numbers. A stranger abandoning prompts must never cost a merchant their own access.

operations.summary: Poll the prompt
operations.description:
Follow the payment until it settles. Scoped to the link, so one link can never read another's order.

A prompt usually resolves in under a minute but can sit unanswered until the rail times it out; poll for a few minutes and then stop rather than spinning forever. On `failed`, show `message` — it is written for the payer and will not accuse them of cancelling unless the rail actually said so.

operations.summary: Collect into the account
operations.description:
Raises a payment prompt on the payer's phone and credits the account when they approve.

Returns as soon as the prompt is out — `status` is `pending` or `processing`, not `completed`. Finish on the `account.collection.completed` webhook or by polling the transaction; the payer may take a minute, or never approve at all.

operations.summary: Preview a disbursement
operations.description:
Cost, total to be debited, and — where the rail supports it — the **resolved recipient name**. Show that name to whoever is approving the payment: it is the one check that catches a wrong number before the money is gone.

Nothing moves.

operations.summary: Disburse from the account
operations.description:
Pays out to a mobile wallet or a bank. The amount plus the fee is **held immediately** against the balance, so a second disbursement cannot spend the same money while the first is in flight.

Returns while the payout is in flight. Finish on `account.disbursement.completed` / `.failed`, or by polling the transaction.

operations.summary: Account statement
operations.description: Opening balance, every movement in the period, closing balance. The reconciliation artefact: the closing balance is derived from the entries rather than read separately, so a statement that balances is evidence the ledger balances.

operations.summary: Get one transaction
operations.description: Look a transaction up directly, without knowing which account it belongs to. Use this after a webhook, or after a `500` where you do not know whether the money moved.

operations.summary: Quote an offramp
operations.description:
Prices crypto → fiat and returns a deposit address.

This is step one of two. Nothing is owed until you send the crypto and submit the hash, and the quote expires — after `expiresAt` the rate is stale and submit is refused, so quote close to when you intend to send.

Send **either** `amount` (how much fiat the recipient should get) **or** `usdcAmount` (how much crypto you want to spend), never both.

operations.summary: Submit the deposit and pay out
operations.description:
Step two. Rift verifies your transaction on-chain, then pays the recipient.

Submitting the same `txHash` twice is safe: the original order is replayed with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Send less than the quote's `sendAmount` and it is refused with `DEPOSIT_TOO_SMALL` rather than partially paid.

operations.summary: Onramp to any address
operations.description:
Collects fiat from a phone and releases crypto to an address you name — a wallet Rift does not hold and has no keys for.

Returns as soon as the prompt is raised. The crypto is sent once the fiat clears; finish on `ramp.onramp.completed` or by polling the order.

operations.description: The order in either direction. This is the source of truth after a webhook, and the thing to call after a `500` when you do not know whether anything happened.

operations.description:
MAW (monthly active wallets) limit enforced per project. optionalApiKey allows API-key-authenticated signups.

**otpCode** — email / phone sign-ups send the code delivered to the identifier being registered (POST /v1/one-time-codes first). Required when sign-up OTP is enforced on the environment; when the flag is off a supplied code is still verified. A verified code leaves a one-time proof (10 min) so the follow-up sign-in with the SAME code succeeds; a proof from POST /otp/verify is also accepted. externalId + password sign-ups do not use otpCode.

API key (X-API-Key) is OPTIONAL on this endpoint — when provided, the project context is attached.

operations.summary: Authenticate existing user.
operations.description:
mode='session' opts into the short-lived JWT + httpOnly refresh-cookie flow.

API key (X-API-Key) is OPTIONAL on this endpoint — when provided, the project context is attached.

This endpoint runs through the **verifyOtp** middleware. The request body must include ONE of:
  • `otpCode` + (`email` OR `phoneNumber`) — passwordless OTP flow (send a code first via POST /v1/one-time-codes), or
  • `externalId` + `password` — for API-key-authenticated projects where the user authenticates with a password.
Without one of these, the endpoint returns 400 with `requiresOTP: true`.
